1) 从告警标签取 upstream 与 name（后端地址），在 Nginx: 1) Take upstream and name (the backend address) from the alert labels and run curl -sv http://<backend address>/ on the Nginx host to confirm it is genuinely unreachable; 2) If it is unreachable, log in to that backend host and confirm the application process and port are alive; 3) If the backend is healthy, check the network and security groups between Nginx and the backend, and whether the probe path in the check directive matches the backend's health check endpoint; 4) Run curl http://<nginx>/status?format=json to see how many nodes are left in the same upstream, and scale out immediately if only one remains.
1) 查看 error_log 是否有 worker_connections a: 1) Check error_log for worker_connections are not enough or too many open files; 2) Estimate the connection ceiling as worker_processes × worker_connections, compare it with the current nginx_active level, and raise worker_connections; 3) Raise worker_rlimit_nofile and the systemd LimitNOFILE to match; 4) Run nginx -s reload and confirm the gap between accepts and handled stops growing.
1) 登录主机执行 systemctl status nginx 或 ps -e: 1) Log in to the host and run systemctl status nginx or ps -ef | grep nginx to confirm the master process is alive; 2) If it is alive, run curl -s http://127.0.0.1/nginx_status to verify by hand whether stub_status is blocked by allow/deny rules or a firewall; 3) If it is not running, validate the config with nginx -t before systemctl start nginx, and read the tail of error_log for the exit reason; 4) Confirm the upstream VIP or load balancer has taken this node out of rotation so traffic stops flowing to it.
Nginx 接受了连接却没能处理完（accepts 与 handled 出现差值: Nginx accepted connections it could not finish handling (a gap between accepts and handled), usually because worker_connections or file handles topped out; some client connections are being dropped outright.
nginx_upstream_check 探测到 upstream 中有后端节点: nginx_upstream_check found a backend node in the upstream marked down; the node has been taken out of rotation, and if nodes in the same upstream keep failing the result is 502s.
